title: When the Yearbook Burns
premise: Quentin Okafor has survived four years at Ashgrove High by being nobody—until her best friend Priya vanishes, leaving behind a janitor's keyring and a half-burned yearbook hidden in the bakery's flour bin. Following the keys into the school's sealed records room, Quentin uncovers a cover-up: years of hushed-up abuse scandals paid off by the school board, with Priya's evidence-gathering as the last loose end. As the board closes in and the school burns its archives for good, Quentin must choose between safety and justice, rallying the silenced students whose stories she can taste in every loaf she bakes. In the end, she broadcasts the truth at graduation through an act of collective memory the board cannot buy back—and Priya, found alive but changed, stands beside her.
about_author: Bram Fairweather is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering school board meetings no one attended. They write young adult fiction about quiet kids who refuse to stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Weight of Flour
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Establishes her invisible life at Ashgrove High and the family bakery where she bakes grief-bread and joy-rolls that people swear they can taste. Priya, her loud, fearless best friend, has been acting strange—asking about old yearbooks, photographing board meeting minutes. Then Priya stops answering texts. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, ending on the discovery of the keyring taped under Priya's locker shelf.

chapters.title: Keys to Rooms That Don't Exist
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Using the keys, she finds the sub-basement archive and Priya's hidden stash: a scorched 1998 yearbook annotated with names of students who 'transferred' after complaints against a beloved coach—complaints settled quietly by the board, including one signed by Quentin's own mother as a young teacher. Rising tension: someone ransacked the archive after her; a black SUV idles outside the bakery. Emotional beat: dread curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Quentin and Priya, held in a motel two towns over, too scared to surface. Quentin tracks down three of the named students—now adults—who confirm everything but beg her to stop; one warns her the board's lawyer destroyed families before. The climax ignites when the board announces an emergency vote to demolish the archive wing, and Quentin realizes the last physical evidence burns Friday. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: Bread for the Whole Town
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with Priya returned. Resolution: instead of fighting the demolition, Quentin bakes all night—loaves embedded with QR codes linking to scanned testimony—and distributes them at graduation, where hundreds of phones light up with the truth simultaneously. The board's chair resigns amid a state investigation; the survivors speak publicly. Priya and Quentin reconcile over burnt cinnamon rolls. Emotional beat: catharsis, justice outside the law, and a girl who was never invisible again.
